prompt: An architect is asked to describe a logistics company's architecture and answers "Java, Oracle and Kafka". By the course, what is missing?
hint: Lesson 2, a technology is not an architecture.

choices.why: Versions make the list longer, not more informative about structure.

choices.text: The elements, how they relate, and what the structure is for
choices.why: Right: the same three tools could build opposite architectures.
One more technology on the list still says nothing about structure.

choices.text: Nothing: those are the architectural choices
choices.why: They may be architectural if expensive to change, but they are not a description of the structure.

prompt: A team adds a reporting service nobody planned. It reads only through other services' public APIs and breaks no rule of the intended design. What is that, in the course's terms?
hint: Lesson 2: does it add, or violate?

choices.why: Right: a decision the plan did not include, without contradicting it.
Erosion violates the intended architecture; this service respects it.
Nothing was designed in advance here; the service arrived unplanned.
The descriptive architecture grew; nothing was corrected.

prompt: A team plans to put Kafka in front of a service that receives 40 small writes per second, "for scale". What does the course recommend checking first?

choices.why: That chooses the technology before checking whether the number demands it.

choices.text: How the team will learn Kafka
choices.why: Learning is a cost of the solution; first find out whether the solution is needed.

choices.text: Whether the load actually needs a broker
choices.why: Right: 40 small writes a second sits well within a single ordinary database.

choices.text: Whether larger companies run Kafka for similar services
choices.why: Other companies' scale is the Netflix argument the course rejects.

prompt: Order these decisions for a new payments feature from the one whose responsible moment comes first to the one that can wait longest.
items: How a repeated payment request is refused
Which team owns the payments data
Which client library calls the bank
The wording of the confirmation e-mail

prompt: By the course, what is the last responsible moment?

choices.text: The latest date on which a decision can still technically be made
choices.why: That is the last possible moment; the responsible one comes before alternatives are lost.

choices.text: When not deciding would eliminate an important alternative
choices.why: Right: before it you guess, after it the code decides for you.

choices.text: The end of the design phase
choices.why: The course rejects architecture as a phase.
It is a property of each decision, not a point in a calendar.

prompt: Match each piece of evidence to what it shows about a running system.
hint: Lesson 2, reading the architecture from the system.

pairs.right: which component can reach which database
which calls actually happen, and in what order
who publishes what, and who listens
which modules depend on which inside one deployable
